And there’s still just a real dearth of power here that even this pitching staff might not be able to make up for.
–CL
8. Philadelphia Phillies
I don’t know what to think of the Philadelphia Phillies. On one hand, a rotation led by Zack Wheeler, Cristopher Sanchez, a healthy Jesus Luzardo, a rejuvenated Aaron Nola and a much-improved Andrew Painter should will them to wins. On the other hand, Luzardo is not healthy, the lineup is top-heavy and the bullpen, outside of Jhoan Duran, is an utter disaster. The Phillies are almost certainly going to make the playoffs, but their losses in New York this week ruined any last hope they had at a division title. And with how they’re playing right now, I don’t know if I’d pick them to get beyond the Wild Card Round.
–ZR
7. Chicago Cubs
The Cubs playoff parade was put on hold Sunday as Alex Bregman was struck in the face by a foul ball. Bregman was taken to the local hospital, and it's unclear how much time he will miss as of this writing. Chicago's postseason hopes may hang in the balance, as their one clear advantage over every other NL team is their lineup. The Cubs have scored the most runs in baseball this year.
-MP
6. San Diego Padres
Yes, the schedule has helped, particularly series against Miami, Colorado, Washington, San Francisco and Cincinnati. But no matter who they've played, the Padres look like a different team from the one we saw for much of the year, with their big bats finally mashing and their rotation coming into focus with Nick Pivetta now back in the fold. San Diego is now dead even with Chicago and Philly in the Wild Card race, and no one will want to face this lineup and this bullpen in a short series.
–CL
5. New York Yankees
Just when it seemed like New York was getting ready to make a move, with Aaron Judge finally back in the lineup after months on the shelf, the reigning AL MVP landed right back on the IL — this time with a calf strain that could well jeopardize his entire postseason. It’s been that sort of year for the Yankees, which have the pitching to keep believing in them as contenders but just haven’t been able to put it all together enough to take command of their own playoff destiny. And with a Judge-less offense and a penchant for mistake-filled baseball, winning three series in a row feels like a tough ask even in this AL.
–CL
4. Atlanta Braves
The Atlanta Braves punched their ticket to the playoffs this week, and thanks to the Phillies’ struggles, they’re on the cusp of winning the NL East — ensuring a top-three seed in the National League. Tyler Mahle pitched another gem, and Ronald Acuña Jr. is hitting his stride at the perfect time. There’re still some concerns with the team, like the No. 3 spot in their rotation and struggling stars like Austin Riley and Ozzie Albies, but getting to the playoffs is a big deal, and the Braves can take pride in checking that box.
–ZR
3. Tampa Bay Rays
The Rays may well have sewn up the AL East this week, taking two of three from the Red Sox over the weekend to stretch their lead over the Yankees ahead of an all-important four-game set in the Bronx beginning on Tuesday. Even if New York were to sweep all four, though, Tampa would still have the inside track to the division and the No. 1 overall seed. This pitching staff continues to thrive beyond all expectation even with some recent injuries, and the hitting has done just enough. Whether that recipe will withstand the postseason is the only question now.
–CL
2. Los Angeles Dodgers
Don't look now, but L.A.'s lineup has begun to stir, with Kyle Tucker looking like the player the Dodgers thought they were paying for this offseason. They also got Edwin Diaz back this week, and he's suddenly looking like the star closer of old — potentially answering this team's biggest question entering October. We know the rotation will be there; if they have Tucker at the height of his powers and a one-two punch in Diaz and Tanner Scott at the end of games, the three-peat march might be back on.
–CL
1. Milwaukee Brewers
The Brewers set a franchise record with 98 wins on Sunday. They still have a full week to go to add to that mark, and appear likely to reach the 100-win plateau. That's a great accomplishment, but it won't mean squat if Milwaukee falls to the Los Angeles Dodgers — or any other NL team for that matter — on their way to that elusive NL pennant. The Brewers are the favorites, but the Dodgers are lingering right behind them.
-MP

title: Cubs somber after Alex Bregman's scary injury
author: Bill Ladson
body:
CINCINNATI -- The Chicago Cubs were somber after they defeated the Cincinnati Reds, 9-1, at Great American Ball Park on Sunday because Chicago was thinking about third baseman Alex Bregman, who was hit in the face by a foul ball off the bat of teammate Michael Busch.
Bregman was injured in the fourth inning with two outs. With the count, 1-2, Busch checked his swing at a pitch thrown by Reds right-hander Luis Mey. The ball made contact with Busch's bat, however, and then hit Bregman while he was in the on-deck circle. Bregman then ran towards the end of the Cubs' dugout before finally going into the clubhouse to get looked at by the team’s trainer.
Bregman was taken to a nearby hospital for X-rays and a CT scan, but the Cubs have yet to announce the seriousness of Bregman’s injury.
“I don’t know anything more than that,” Cubs manager Craig Counsell told reporters. “He had a cut under his eye. He was bleeding from his nose a little bit. It’s pretty swollen. It was below the eye. I honestly thought it hit him in the nose. I thought he had a broken nose, but I knew it hit him somewhere in the face. It’s just an unfortunate accident. I’m hoping and praying he is all right.
“We have to get good results from the hospital first. [Bregman] got hit in the face, so you are worried about his general well-being first. If we get a good report, we’ll move to the next step. I want to get a good report.”
Bregman is in his first season with the Cubs after signing a five-year, $175 million contract last January. He is having a productive season with the Cubbies, slashing .262/.352/.452 with 26 home runs and 89 RBI.
Before Sunday’s game, Bregman spoke to Yardbarker about his first season with the Cubs.
"The first half didn’t start out how I wanted it. (I) kept fighting. (I) trusted the process,” Bregman said. “I felt like myself over the last two months. That’s what I expect from myself. I’ve also been super thrilled to be in a position to continue to play postseason baseball, play meaningful games in October. I’ve been fortunate to do that every year of my career, which I don’t take lightly. I’m happy that we put ourselves in the position, so far, to be in.”
Bregman even had a word to say about teammate Pete Crow-Armstrong. To Bregman, PCA is the National League Most Valuable Player, and he has the stats to back it up.
Entering Tuesday’s action against the Marlins, Crow-Armstrong is leading the Majors with 10.5 wins above replacement (per FanGraphs) and 118 runs scored. He could also become the seventh player in MLB history to reach the 40-40 plateau.
“He has been the best player in the sport. It’s not even close,” Bregman said about PCA.
All quotations obtained firsthand unless otherwise noted.

title: Why Paul Skenes blames the World Baseball Classic for decreased velocity as Pirates ace wraps up down season
author: Mike Axisa
body:
Despite an active offseason and a busy trade deadline, the Pittsburgh Pirates were officially eliminated from postseason contention this past weekend. At 79-77, they have a chance to finish with a winning record for the first time since 2018, but that is the smallest of consolations. The Pirates made moves intending to contend this year, but missed the postseason.
One reason -- maybe the biggest reason, but not the only reason -- that the Pirates missed the postseason is a down year by reigning Cy Young winner Paul Skenes. A down year that included some outright bad stretches. Skenes has a 3.91 ERA in 168 innings this season, but from May 17 to July 31, he had a 14-start stretch with a 5.18 ERA. Pittsburgh went 3-11 in those 14 games.
Over the weekend, Skenes acknowledged that the World Baseball Classic may have contributed to his fluctuating velocity and down year because it interrupted his usual spring training buildup.
"There are a lot of other factors, so I don't want to put everything on that, but I feel like that was kind of the root of it a little bit," Skenes told the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette. "Usually that time of year, you're kind of ramping up and it's a little bit slow. You can kind of get onto the slope and find your body. One live (batting practice), you're topping at 97, and then the next you're 98, 99. And that wasn't the case this year. Looking back, I don't think that really helped."
Skenes made two starts for Team USA in the WBC, which has strict pitch limits and rest requirements, and allowed one run in 8 ⅓ innings. He did not make it out of the first inning on Opening Day, in part because his defense betrayed him, then Skenes put together a dominant eight-start stretch in which he pitched to a 1.09 ERA and averaged over six innings per start.
The rough stretch began after that, as did the velocity decline. And to be clear, Skenes still threw very hard. There were just more 95s and 96s and fewer 98s and 99s. Overall, Skenes averaged 96.8 mph with his fastball this year, down from 98.2 mph last year and 98.9 mph the year before that. He did not throw a single 100 mph pitch for the first time in his three MLB seasons.
"I didn't really have a number on it, but I would have liked to throw harder than I have this year," Skenes told the Post-Gazette. "Unfortunately, it's probably going to take an offseason to get (the velocity) back. Yeah, it's just tough."
The single most important thing is health and there's no chance -- zero -- the Pirates would have allowed Skenes to continue taking the ball every fifth day if there was a known injury. More than anything, his mechanics seemed out of whack, and mechanical fixes aren't always quick and easy, especially in-season. How much the WBC contributed to that, we don't know, but Skenes believes it was a factor.
Several other pitchers who participated in the WBC have had down years, including Skenes' USA teammate Logan Webb, but there's also a long list of pitchers who have thrived after the WBC. Nolan McLean, Eduardo Rodriguez, Cristopher Sánchez, and Yoshinobu Yamamoto are among them. They played in the WBC and have been among baseball's best pitchers in 2026.
Skenes, 24, is 14th among all pitchers in WAR despite his down season. He is looking at a record payday for a pitcher in his first year of arbitration eligibility this offseason. Skenes will become a free agent after the 2029 season.

title: Could Boston Red Sox Target Randy Arozarena in Free Agency?
author: Zach Coe
body:
RedSoxRoundtable's Zach Coe discusses whether or not the Red Sox have enough offensive firepower to win a World Series on the 'Bleav in Boston' podcast. Be sure to join our FREE community over on RedSoxRoundtable.com!
The Boston Red Sox have a well-documented outfield logjam, with Jarren Duran, Ceddanne Rafaela, Wilyer Abreu, and Roman Anthony. But could the team be preparing to add another piece to the already confusing puzzle? At least one person thinks so, as Seattle Mariners beat reporter Ryan Divish linked pending free-agent Randy Arozarena to Boston in an appearance on the 'Foul Territory' podcast.
What did Divish say?
"They're [Seattle] going to lose their best player. Randy Arozarena is going to be a free agent. I think we all know Randy would probably prefer to stay on the East Coast," Divish said. "I'm guessing Boston is ready to cut a huge check for him," he continued.
Is Arozarena a fit?
From a sheer production perspective, the 31-year-old could be the missing piece for a Red Sox offense that still feels a bat short. Arozarena is coming off the best two seasons of his career, hitting .258/.355/.453/.808 with 53 home runs, 63 doubles, and 152 RBI en route to back-to-back All-Star selections, all while playing half of his games in one of the most pitcher-friendly environments in the sport, Seattle's T-Mobile Park.
Arozarena has also had incredible success at Fenway Park, posting a .278/.351/.481/.833 slash line with five home runs, 12 doubles, and 19 RBI in career 32 games. He also fits the profile of hitters that Boston has targeted under Chief Baseball Officer Craig Breslow, pulling the ball in the air at a consistent rate. Along with a strong track record at Fenway Park, Arozarena has proven himself in the postseason, hitting .292/.380/.565/.946 in 45 playoff games, including being named ALCS Most Valuable Player in 2020 with the Tampa Bay Rays.
However, bringing in the veteran outfielder would require significant roster reshuffling, including moving both an outfielder and the designated hitter, Masataka Yoshida.
Our take
If Arozarena is set on returning to the East Coast, he could be the perfect fit for the Red Sox offense. His defensive metrics at this stage of his career suggest he's best suited as a designated hitter, and the Red Sox have gotten some of the worst production in baseball from their revolving door of designated hitters in 2026. He also has a proven track record of success at both Fenway Park and in the postseason.
While signing him would require some roster maneuvering, including potentially selling Duran at his lowest possible value or eating the $18.6 million remaining on Masataka Yoshida's contract, Arozarena is about as perfect fit as you can get for the Red Sox in what's set to be a weak class of free-agent bats, especially if the offense comes up short in the playoffs for the second consecutive season.
Up next for the Sox
After clinching a playoff berth on Sunday afternoon, the Red Sox are off on Monday before opening up the final homestand of the regular season on Tuesday, welcoming the Cleveland Guardians to Fenway Park for a three-game set. Payton Tolle (9-6, 3.02 ERA) will get the start opposite fellow rookie left-hander Parker Messick (12-9, 2.57 ERA) for Cleveland. First pitch is set for 6:45 p.m. ET.

Arozarena is coming off the best two seasons of his career, hitting .258/.355/.453/.808 with 53 home runs, 63 doubles, and 152 RBI en route to back-to-back All-Star selections, all while playing half of his games in one of the most pitcher-friendly environments in the sport, Seattle's T-Mobile Park.
Arozarena has also had incredible success at Fenway Park, posting a .278/.351/.481/.833 slash line with five home runs, 12 doubles, and 19 RBI in career 32 games. He also fits the profile of hitters that Boston has targeted under Chief Baseball Officer Craig Breslow, pulling the ball in the air at a consistent rate. Along with a strong track record at Fenway Park, Arozarena has proven himself in the postseason, hitting .292/.380/.565/.946 in 45 playoff games, including being named ALCS Most Valuable Player in 2020 with the Tampa Bay Rays.
However, bringing in the veteran outfielder would require significant roster reshuffling, including moving both an outfielder and the designated hitter, Masataka Yoshida.
Our take
If Arozarena is set on returning to the East Coast, he could be the perfect fit for the Red Sox offense. His defensive metrics at this stage of his career suggest he's best suited as a designated hitter, and the Red Sox have gotten some of the worst production in baseball from their revolving door of designated hitters in 2026. He also has a proven track record of success at both Fenway Park and in the postseason.
While signing him would require some roster maneuvering, including potentially selling Duran at his lowest possible value or eating the $18.6 million remaining on Masataka Yoshida's contract, Arozarena is about as perfect fit as you can get for the Red Sox in what's set to be a weak class of free-agent bats, especially if the offense comes up short in the playoffs for the second consecutive season.
Up next for the Sox
After clinching a playoff berth on Sunday afternoon, the Red Sox are off on Monday before opening up the final homestand of the regular season on Tuesday, welcoming the Cleveland Guardians to Fenway Park for a three-game set. Payton Tolle (9-6, 3.02 ERA) will get the start opposite fellow rookie left-hander Parker Messick (12-9, 2.57 ERA) for Cleveland. First pitch is set for 6:45 p.m. ET.

title: Tarik Skubal Explains Viral Outburst in Dodgers Dugout
author: Noah Camras; Unknown
body:
Tarik Skubal didn't have his best stuff on Saturday night against the San Francisco Giants.
He let his anger out on the Los Angeles Dodgers dugout.
Amid his worst start as a Dodger on Saturday at UNIQLO Field at Dodger Stadium, Skubal was seen having a mini outburst in the team's dugout between innings.
Skubal removed his glove and hat and threw them at the bench. He then picked up a bottle and flung it at the wall before sitting down, getting back up and walking down to the clubhouse.
After the game, Skubal was asked about that moment, and explained what happened.
“Sometimes you get frustrated and you got to get it out,” Skubal said to reporters. “It’s no good just keeping it pent up. So yeah, I’m a believer in getting that stuff out and kind of just moving on from the moment. The frustration is based on execution and knowing who I am and I’m just not doing that.”
Skubal was not happy with his performance, and understandably so. Against a weak San Francisco Giants lineup, the left-hander allowed four runs — his most since being acquired ahead of the trade deadline — on eight hits with just three strikeouts, his fewest in nine starts with LA.
Skubal hadn't allowed four runs in a game since June 24. He hadn't had fewer than four strikeouts since April 1.
“Fastball command wasn’t great,” he said of what went wrong. “Not driving it up and in, kind of pulling the ball down at times, pushing it up at times. I think almost [all] pitching is all fastball command, and mine wasn’t great today.”
Fortunately, the Dodgers offense picked Skubal up, as they scored 10 runs and even put him in line for the win, his fourth as a Dodger. However, after coming off his best start with LA, the reigning two-time Cy Young award winner was looking for better results.
Skubal should make one more start in the regular season before likely starting one of the team's first two games in the postseason.
The two-time All-Star only has six career postseason starts under his belt, all coming over the last two years with the Detroit Tigers.
Overall, Skubal has a 2.04 ERA with 56 strikeouts to six walks over 39.2 postseason innings. He has completed at least six innings in all six of his starts.

title: Chicago Cubs update: Pete Crow-Armstrong, David Peterson, Daniel Palencia
author: Al Yellon
body:
With one week to go in the regular season, the Cubs' magic number to clinch a postseason berth has dropped to one, and their magic number to get home field in a Wild Card series is now six. This means that the Cubs control their own destiny. Win out — six games — and they will be home a week from Tuesday against either the Padres or Phillies. (Easy? No, but it is possible.)
In the meantime, here's who was hot and not for the Cubs over the past week.
Three up
Pete Crow-Armstrong had a very weird, but productive, week
PCA batted .345/.367/.897 (10-for-29) with two doubles, a triple, four home runs, nine RBI, seven runs scored and two stolen bases. That's a 1.264 OPS for the six games, which might actually be good enough to get him another Player of the Week award.
But here's the thing. He put up those numbers while going 0-for-15 with five strikeouts in three of the six games!
That means that in the other three games, he was 10-for-14 (.714) with all those other peripheral numbers.
That's just crazy. Here's his 3-for-4 day against the Braves last Wednesday [VIDEO].
Your browser does not support the video tag.
I keep saying this but I have to say it one more time: Savor this PCA season, we have not seen anything like it from a Cubs player — or most MLB players! — in most of our lifetimes. I hope he can steal two bases against the Marlins this week so he'd join the 40/40 club at Wrigley Field.
And remember, PCA is only 24. Who knows? He might do this again next year!
David Peterson is getting hot at just the right time
In his two starts over the week ending Sunday, Peterson threw 12 innings, allowed six hits and two runs, walked four and struck out 14. For his last three starts, which include two against postseason teams (Braves and Brewers), Peterson has a 1.65 ERA and 1.163 WHIP and 18 strikeouts in 16.1 innings. (And the run charged to him against Atlanta scored after he left the game.)
I think the Cubs might have to consider Peterson for a Wild Card series start.
Your browser does not support the video tag.
Daniel Palencia appears to be back
Palencia pitched just twice over the week, but the second outing was two scoreless innings against the Reds Saturday, the first time he'd thrown two full innings in a game since April 2025. The best news is that in that two-inning outing, Palencia threw eight of his 20 pitches at 100 miles per hour, a level he had trouble hitting in his first few outings back.
Your browser does not support the video tag.
I don't think I have to tell you how much having a productive Palencia would mean for the Cubs in the postseason.
Three down
Nico Hoerner is still struggling
Remember when Nico was hitting at MVP level in April?
He's had a rough time since then. Over the six games he batted just .250/.280/.292 (6-for-24) with one double.
Nico's offensive numbers are down this year and he's only going to post a bit more than 2 bWAR after a 6.2 bWAR season in 2025.
Hopefully he can turn it on in October, and continue playing solid defense at second base.
Clay Holmes got roughed up by the Reds
Holmes has had a couple of clunkers since joining the Cubs — this week against the Reds and the previous week against the Marlins.
The good news is that both of those starts were on the road. In four Wrigley Field starts since joining the Cubs, Holmes has a 1.14 ERA and 1.014 WHIP in 23.2 innings, with 18 strikeouts and only one home run allowed.
He'll likely start Thursday against the Marlins (though currently that game is listed as TBD for the Cubs starter), which would set him up for a start in the Wild Card series the following week. If that series winds up at Wrigley, I'd seriously consider Holmes for one of the starts.
Edward Cabrera had a rough transition to relieving, but maybe there's hope
Cabrera's first relief outing for the Cubs probably went an inning too long, as he was left in for a third inning of work after finishing the seventh and throwing a scoreless eighth against the Braves last Wednesday. Craig Counsell left him out there in a 4-3 game and he served up a two-run homer to Drake Baldwin in the ninth.
Things were better for Cabrera in a scoreless inning against the Reds in a low-leverage situation on Sunday. He allowed a hit and a walk, but got out of the inning with a double play. He threw only nine pitches, two of which hit 99. Perhaps shorter outings would be better for Cabrera.

title: Paul Skenes Blames WBC Play for Affecting Velocity Drop in 2026 MLB Season
author: Scott Polacek
body:
Paul Skenes Blames WBC Play for Affecting Velocity Drop in 2026 MLB Season
Paul Skenes' drop in velocity has been a major storyline surrounding the Pittsburgh Pirates this season, and he placed some of the blame on pitching in the World Baseball Classic.
"There are a lot of other factors, so I don't want to put everything on that," the Pittsburgh Pirates ace said, per Colin Beazley of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette. "But I feel like that was kind of the root of it a little bit."
He said the drop in velocity was initially intentional, but he was never able to fully ramp up to his typical level.
"Usually, that time of year, you're kind of ramping up and it's a little bit slow," Skenes explained. "You can kind of get onto the slope and find your body. One live [batting practice], you're topping at 97 [mph], and then the next you're 98, 99. And that wasn't the case this year. ... Looking back, I don't think that really helped."
Skenes has still been solid this season with a 3.91 ERA, 1.13 WHIP and 192 strikeouts in 168 innings. In fact, the vast majority of the starting pitchers across the league would take those numbers.
But the vast majority of the pitchers across the league aren't Skenes.
The right-hander broke onto the major league scene in 2024 as the National League Rookie of the Year who finished third in Cy Young voting with a 1.96 ERA, 0.95 WHIP and 170 strikeouts in 133 innings.
He was even better in his second year as the NL Cy Young winner with a 1.97 ERA, 0.95 WHIP and 216 strikeouts in 187.2 innings. Seeing how that was his age-23 season, it was realistic to expect continued dominance for the foreseeable future.
However, he hasn't been the same in 2026 in part because of the drop in velocity.
Beazley noted Skenes averaged 98.8 mph on his fastball as a rookie and 98.1 in his second year. By comparison, his average this season is 96.8 mph.
Codify highlighted the recent fall off in his starts:
Fortunately for Skenes and the Pirates, he is still just 24 years old with plenty of time to bounce back. He also admitted he didn't train with a specific velocity in mind for the 2026 campaign, which was an unusual one that started earlier because of the World Baseball Classic.
There is no WBC in 2027, meaning he can go through a normal offseason and spring training ramp-up before taking the mound in his fourth season.
Perhaps that will help Skenes return to being one of the best pitchers in baseball like he was during his first two seasons.

title: San Francisco Giants Announce Marcelo Mayer News Before Twins Series
author: Ben Stinar
body:
On Monday, the San Francisco Giants will open up a series with the Minnesota Twins at Oracle Park in California.
They are coming off a series where they got swept by the Los Angeles Dodgers (on the road).
San Francisco Giants Announce Marcelo Mayer News
Ahead of their series with the Twins, the Giants announced news about Marcelo Mayer.

title: Mike Trout net worth in 2026: LA Angels salary, MLB career earnings, endorsements, investments and lifestyle
author: Global Sports Desk
body:
Mike Trout has spent his entire MLB career with the Los Angeles Angels, going from the first overall pick in the draft to one of the most recognisable stars in baseball. That career has been mirrored by his financial profile, with the bulk of his publicly known earnings from football coming through long-term contracts.
Trout is still under the massive extension he signed with the Los Angeles Angels in 2019 through 2026. The deal runs up to and including the end of the 2030 season and still pays a healthy annual salary, with his commercial relationships and investment interests providing other sources of income.
Mike Trout net worth and Los Angeles Angels earnings
Public estimates vary regarding Mike Trout's net worth because private investments, taxes, spending and other personal assets are not fully disclosed. Reports estimating Trout’s net worth at around $220 million in 2026 have cited Celebrity Net Worth. That figure should be viewed as an estimate, not an independently audited accounting of his assets.
That wealth stems from Trout’s MLB pay. Celebrity Net Worth reports Spotrac listing his 2026 cash salary at $35.45 million, but his payroll figure is about $37.12 million because of contract accounting. His 2019 extension is for $426.5 million over 12 years with an average annual value of roughly $35.54 million.

| 2026 payroll figure | $37.12 million |

| Contract through | 2030 | 
| Average annual value | $35.54 million | 
Mike Trout’s historic contract remains his financial foundation
The centrepiece to Trout’s earning power in MLB is his current 12-year, $426.5 million deal with the Los Angeles Angels. The deal was done in March 2019 and extends through the 2030 season, providing Trout with guaranteed long-term financial security with the organization. It also features a full no-trade clause and no opt-outs.
The deal comes with a $35.45 million cash salary for 2026. Spotrac’s contract breakdown reveals the same $35.45 million base figure for every year through 2030, while the payroll value is closer to $37.12 million each season because of the allocation of his signing bonus.
Trout’s total MLB cash earnings have also reached a milestone. Based on those figures, his cash earnings through 2026 are roughly $338.64 million. Spotrac lists his career earnings through the 2025 season at $303.19 million, and his 2026 salary at another $35.45 million.

Mike Trout endorsements and investments add off-field wealth
Trout’s earning power goes beyond his Los Angeles Angels salary through a portfolio of commercial partnerships developed during his MLB career. One of his biggest brand relationships has been with Nike, which has previously given Trout a signature shoe line. His perennial baseball star status has also made him attractive to companies across sports, fitness and consumer markets.
Another important chapter in the financial history of Trout is BODYARMOR. Trout was an investor and ambassador for the sports-drink brand, as was Kobe Bryant, an early major shareholder. In 2018, Coca-Cola Company acquired a minority stake in BODYARMOR and in 2021 announced it would buy the remaining 85% for $5.6 billion. Public accounts have linked Trout to the firm’s original cohort of investors, although the exact amount of his personal earnings has not been publicly disclosed.
Mike Trout’s overall financial picture for 2026 largely hinges on his long-term deal with the Los Angeles Angels and an estimated $338 million in MLB cash earnings through the 2026 season, with his wealth outside of baseball buoyed by endorsements and investments.

title: ¡Drama en las Grandes Ligas! Alex Bregman queda con el rostro desfigurado tras pelotazo en la MLB
author: Yunior Carteño
body:
Un momento completamente accidental encendió las alarmas en las Grandes Ligas. Alex Bregman, tercera base de los Chicago Cubs, terminó en el hospital después de recibir un fuerte pelotazo en el rostro durante el juego contra los Cincinnati Reds, pese a que ni siquiera se encontraba bateando cuando ocurrió el impacto.
¿Cómo ocurrió el accidente de Alex Bregman?
El incidente se produjo este domingo 20 de septiembre en el Great American Ball Park, cuando Michael Busch estaba en la caja ante los lanzamientos del dominicano Luis Mey. El pelotero de Chicago realizó un swing contenido y alcanzó a desviar la bola de foul, que tomó una trayectoria inesperada hacia donde Bregman esperaba su turno.
Con dos outs en la cuarta entrada, la pelota golpeó directamente a Bregman en el pómulo izquierdo, debajo del ojo. El antesalista reaccionó inmediatamente, soltó su bat y caminó hacia el dugout mientras se cubría la zona afectada con una mano.
La escena generó preocupación entre sus compañeros debido a la fuerza y ubicación del impacto. El manager de los Cubs, Craig Counsell, reveló posteriormente que el jugador presentaba una cortada debajo del ojo, inflamación y también sangrado por la nariz.
“Es un accidente terrible. Esperamos que esté bien”, señaló el estratega, quien admitió que inicialmente creyó que su pelotero podía tener la nariz fracturada debido a la violencia del golpe.
Chicago decidió retirarlo inmediatamente del encuentro. Matt Shaw entró como bateador emergente, mientras Pedro Ramírez posteriormente pasó a cubrir la tercera base. Los Cubs terminaron imponiéndose 9-1 sobre Cincinnati.
Alex Bregman fue trasladado al hospital
Debido a que la bola alcanzó una zona particularmente delicada, Bregman fue enviado a un hospital para someterse a radiografías y una tomografía computarizada (CT) con el objetivo de conocer la gravedad de la lesión y descartar daños mayores.
Michael Busch reconoció que continuar jugando después del episodio resultó complicado. El beisbolista explicó que todo sucedió en cuestión de segundos y manifestó su preocupación debido a que cualquier golpe en la cabeza genera alarma dentro del diamante.
Horas después, el propio Bregman dio señales alentadoras mediante sus redes sociales. El estadounidense publicó una fotografía donde apareció con el ojo izquierdo completamente inflamado, moretones y restos de sangre alrededor del rostro, una imagen que evidenció la fuerza del impacto.
Pese a lo aparatoso de su aspecto, acompañó la publicación con un breve mensaje para tranquilizar a sus seguidores: “Gracias por todos los mensajes. Volveré”.
El accidente llegó además durante una campaña importante para Bregman con los Cubs. El tercera base registra promedio de .262, 26 cuadrangulares y 89 carreras impulsadas en la temporada 2026, por lo que su evolución médica será seguida de cerca por Chicago en la recta final de la campaña.

title: Paul Skenes Reveals Whether World Baseball Classic Is To Blame For Down Year
author: Aaliyan Mohammed
body:
Paul Skenes won the National League Cy Young Award last year, but has not had his best season this year.
Skenes was the National League Rookie of the Year in 2024, and looked like the best pitcher in baseball coming into the season. Through 55 career starts, he had a 1.96 ERA and 386 strikeouts. However, thgis year, he has a 3.91 ERA and his velocity is down. While every fan wonders what has happened to Skenes, he noted that the quick ramp-up for the World Baseball Classic may have played a role.
"There are a lot of other factors, so I don't want to put everything on that," Skenes told the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette's Colin Beazley. "But I feel like that was kind of the root of it a little bit."
"Usually, that time of year, you're kind of ramping up and it's a little bit slow. You can kind of get onto the slope and find your body," Skenes added. "One live (batting practice), you're topping at 97 (mph), and then the next you're 98, 99. And that wasn't the case this year. ... Looking back, I don't think that really helped."
Skenes made two starts in the World Baseball Classic, allowing one earned run in 8 1/3 innings of work. He was brilliant on the biggest stage, but perhaps the intensity of the event without a proper spring training build-up ended up hurting his numbers.
In 2024, his average fastball velocity was 98.8 mph. Last season it was 98.2 mph. This year, his four-seamer is sitting at 96.8 mph. It's a significant drop-off, but perhaps a full offseason with proper spring training will get him back on track next season.
"It definitely affected the year," Skenes said of the World Baseball Classic. "Unfortunately, I don't think I'm the only one."

In 2024, his average fastball velocity was 98.8 mph. Last season it was 98.2 mph. This year, his four-seamer is sitting at 96.8 mph. It's a significant drop-off, but perhaps a full offseason with proper spring training will get him back on track next season.
"It definitely affected the year," Skenes said of the World Baseball Classic. "Unfortunately, I don't think I'm the only one."

title: Here's the Latest on Injury to Seattle Mariners Closer Andres Munoz
author: Brady Farkas
body:
The Mariners beat the Colorado Rockies 2-1 on Sunday, but the closer left the game in the bottom of the ninth inning. Here's what we know, and what could be coming, as well as who could replace him for the rest of the year.
As the Mariners effectively play out the string in a disappointing year, it was a nice way to end a road trip.
However, it wasn't all nice: After allowing a solo home run and a walk in the bottom of the ninth inning, closer Andres Munoz left the game with manager Dan Wilson and the medical staff.
The hard-throwing closer will get imaging done on Monday and the team will see what's going on. Munoz says he's dealt with this issue before, though it's not something we've really heard about.
What's next?
Well, the Mariners are not officially eliminated from the playoff race yet, as they trail the Texas Rangers by five games in the American League West race with six games to play. As a result, they probably want to put their best foot forward until they are eliminated, so they'd certainly like to have Munoz available for the two-game series against the Houston Astros that begins on Tuesday.
But, the Mariners also have to be realistic about where they are at. If there is even a shred of a doubt that Munoz is not OK, they should be willing to shut him down and get him a head start the offseason. Munoz has pitched a lot in the last several years. He's made 60 appearances or more in four of the last five seasons. He also pitched deep into the postseason in 2025 and appeared in the 2026 World Baseball Classic.
Who would close in his absence?
Well, it will likely depend on multiple factors, namely - if the Mariners are still involved in the race or not. Eduard Bazardo, who got the save on Sunday after Munoz left, could get a crack at it. Furthermore, Jose Ferrer, who has three saves this year, has some closing experience. He picked up 11 saves for the Washington Nationals a season ago before getting traded to the Mariners.
Gabe Speier could also get opportunities.
Up next
The Mariners are off on Monday before beginning that series against the Astros at T-Mobile Park. It's just a two-game series before the Mariners close things out with the Los Angeles Angels from Thursday-Sunday.

title: Who needs to step up if Cubs make a run in October?
author: Jackson Stone
body:
The Cubs are as close to securing a trip back to the postseason as possible.
The North Siders need just a single win, or a single D-backs loss, over the regular season’s final week to clinch a spot in the NL Wild Card round.
Who will the Cubs play? And where will those games be played? Those questions won’t be answered until next weekend, most likely.
But with just six games remaining until playoff baseball, who will the Cubs need to step up in order to make a run at the World Series in a National League field filled with strong contenders such as the Brewers, Dodgers and Braves?
Here’s a look at who the Cubs need to do their part to get back to the Fall Classic for the first time since 2016:
Who will step up at the back end of the 'pen?
Who will close games? This is by far the Cubs’ biggest, and potentially most important, question that needs to be answered. Will it be Jacob Webb, who leads the team with nine saves, or will former closer Daniel Palencia, who just spun two scoreless innings in one of his most impressive outings of the year, be able to take that role? Manager Craig Counsell, who has used 14 pitchers to record saves this season, will be tasked with piecing together a bullpen that has limited experience in those situations.
The Cubs need Webb, who spun a scoreless outing in 24 straight appearances from June to August, to get back into form after allowing 11 runs over his past 7 2/3 innings (nine games). If Palencia, who has thrown 6 1/3 straight scoreless innings, can also replicate his success from 2025, it could be a major boost for a club that entered Cincinnati converting just four of its past 12 save opportunities.
Deadline acquisition Ryan Zeferjahn and lefty Ryan Rolison could also play a big factor late in games, but there’s also a secret weapon waiting out in the bullpen …
Can Cabrera be a reliable relief option?
That brings us to Edward Cabrera, who returned from a recurring blister injury on his pitching hand on Sept. 15 in a multi-inning relief role. That will be his job going forward as the Cubs hope shorter outings can not only keep him healthy, but potentially provide a small uptick in velocity. Cabrera’s first relief experience had mixed results (two runs in 2 1/3 IP), but he came out of the bullpen Sunday and tossed a scoreless inning on just nine pitches.
The best-case scenario of this temporary move to the bullpen? Cabrera turns into this year’s version of the Dodgers’ Roki Sasaki, which would immediately help stabilize the back end of the Cubs’ bullpen. Cabrera’s season hasn’t gone to plan, posting a 5.68 ERA in 15 starts between three stints on the injured list, but he still has a chance to make a significant impact when it matters most.
PCA still doing MVP things in October
Is it really fair to ask more of Pete Crow-Armstrong? After going yard again Sunday, the Cubs slugger is tied with Philadelphia’s Kyle Schwarber for the most home runs in the Major Leagues. He leads Chicago in batting average (.280), homers (45), RBIs (107), stolen bases (38), runs scored (118), on-base percentage (.371), hits (170), triple (eight) and games played (156). Got all that? Simply put, he’s put together one of the most impressive offensive seasons in Cubs history and he’s not done.
But he will need others to contribute in October. While run production starts with Crow-Armstrong, even if he performs to his NL MVP front-runner ability, he can’t do it all himself. The North Siders have to count on Seiya Suzuki, Dansby Swanson, Ian Happ, Alex Bregman and Michael Busch below him in the lineup to generate scoring chances.
Holmes stepping up as playoff ace
Clay Holmes and Matthew Boyd are the clear No. 1 and No. 2 options for the playoffs, but Counsell hasn’t yet revealed who will pitch in the all-important Game 1. Holmes had a strong August (1.55 ERA in five starts) in his return to the big leagues after missing nearly three months with a right fibula fracture, but he’s allowed 16 ER in just 15 1/3 IP across three starts in September (9.39 ERA).
That’s a worrying trend for a club with limited starting options in the postseason, but Shota Imanaga has stabilized recently after a down stretch in August, and veteran Kevin Gausman can provide multiple innings in whatever role the Cubs need during the postseason.

title: Bobby Witt Jr. and the Off-Peak MVP Season
author: Davy Andrews
body:
Bobby Witt Jr. is having a down year. He’s running his worst batting line in three seasons. He’s in danger of missing the 20-homer threshold for the first time in his career. A lower back injury in July will also limit him to a career low in games played. Put it together, and Witt is on pace to put up his the lowest WAR total since his 5.9-win 2023 campaign. Oh, and he also grabbed hold of the American League lead in WAR back in July and still hasn’t relinquished it. A down year by Bobby Witt Jr.’s standards is still good enough to make him a deserving MVP.
I don’t know if Witt is going to win his first MVP this year. Ours is the only flavor of WAR in which he leads the AL, and he leads by just a quarter of a win. He ranks third by Baseball Reference’s rWAR and is eighth by Baseball Prospectus’ WARP. Yordan Alvarez leads all of baseball in WARP because he’s hitting like, well, Yordan Alvarez and staying healthy like, well, someone other than Yordan Alvarez. Cam Schlittler leads the AL in Baseball Reference WAR, and he’s been so dominant that he deserves consideration for the Cy Young-MVP combo — if only he’d pitched just 23 fewer innings last year, he could’ve gone for the trifecta with Rookie of the Year. Kevin McGonigle has played like an MVP from the moment he arrived in Detroit, and Junior Caminero has surpassed 40 home runs for the second season in a row as a 23-year-old. All of these guys have a case, and they aren’t the only ones who merit inclusion in the discussion:
| Name | fWAR Rk | fWAR | rWAR Rk | rWAR | WARP Rk | WARP | Avg Rk | Avg WAR | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bobby Witt Jr. | 1 | 6.6 | 3 | 6.5 | 8 | 5 | 4 | 6.0 | 
| Yordan Alvarez | 2 | 6.4 | 4 | 6.4 | 1 | 7.3 | 2 | 6.7 | 
| Cam Schlittler | 3 | 6.1 | 1 | 7 | 3 | 5.8 | 2 | 6.3 | 
| Dylan Cease | 4 | 5.5 | 8 | 5.7 | 12 | 4.6 | 8 | 5.3 | 
| Miguel Vargas | 5 | 5.2 | 10 | 5.3 | 2 | 5.9 | 6 | 5.5 | 
| Junior Caminero | 6 | 5.2 | 7 | 5.7 | 5 | 5.3 | 6 | 5.4 | 
| Kevin McGonigle | 7 | 5.1 | 2 | 6.7 | 4 | 5.3 | 4 | 5.7 | 
| Randy Arozarena | 8 | 5.1 | 11 | 5.3 | 16 | 4 | 12 | 4.8 | 
| Dillon Dingler | 9 | 4.6 | 25 | 4 | 23 | 3.3 | 19 | 4.0 | 
| Drew Rasmussen | 10 | 4.6 | 21 | 4.2 | 13 | 4.4 | 15 | 4.4 | 
| Reid Detmers | 11 | 4.6 | 35 | 3.7 | 11 | 4.7 | 19 | 4.3 | 
| Parker Messick | 13 | 4.6 | 6 | 5.8 | 9 | 4.8 | 9 | 5.1 | 
| Pete Alonso | 14 | 4.2 | 18 | 4.3 | 6 | 5.3 | 13 | 4.6 | 
| Ceddanne Rafaela | 21 | 3.9 | 9 | 5.4 | 94 | 1.7 | 41 | 3.7 | 
| Gavin Williams | 27 | 3.7 | 46 | 3.1 | 7 | 5.2 | 27 | 4.0 | 
| Wilyer Abreu | 32 | 3.4 | 5 | 5.8 | 20 | 3.6 | 19 | 4.3 | 
| Mike Trout | 40 | 3.2 | 28 | 3.9 | 10 | 4.8 | 26 | 4.0 | 
Pete Crow-Armstrong, Jacob Misiorowski, Schlittler, McGonigle and JJ Wetherholt have made the AL MVP the only major award that’s really in question). If you want to read a particularly good example, you should check out the one Mario Delgado Genzor wrote for Baseball Prospectus on Friday. I want to focus on something slightly different — namely, how good Witt has already been in years when he missed out on an MVP and how unusual it would be for him to win it this year.
(A quick note before we get into it: We’re about to spend a lot of time talking about WAR. I know I mentioned rWAR and WARP earlier. They’re an important piece of the puzzle, especially due to the outsized effect rWAR in particular has on the MVP conversation, but from here on out, we’re sticking with good old FanGraphs WAR.)
This is Witt’s fifth major league season, and you could argue that it’s his fourth consecutive MVP-caliber campaign. Mind you, that argument would focus only on 2022, in which he put up 5.9 WAR, good for 10th in the majors. There’s no argument to be had about the 2024 and 2025 seasons. That said, along with Shohei Ohtani’s combined 9.2-WAR 2022 sesaon, they are the two most valuable seasons this decade for which a position player did not win an MVP. In 2024, Witt ran a 169 wRC+, stole 31 bases, and put up a Fielding Run Value of 11, fourth among all shortstops. That was good for 10.5 WAR, and it took the best season of Aaron Judge’s career – 58 home runs, a 19% walk rate, and a .322 batting average – to beat him. In 2025, Witt put up 8.0 WAR with a 130 wRC+, 38 steals, and 20 FRV, the best mark among all shortstops. Again, he was bested by a 10-win season from Judge and Cal Raleigh’s 60-homer campaign. Witt has never received a first place MVP vote.
Crow-Armstrong, who has the National League MVP all but locked down, gives us a great example of what it normally takes to win an MVP award. He may even finish with 10.5 WAR through his excellence in all three phases of the game, just like Witt did in 2024. Players like Judge, Ohtani, and Mike Trout, whose base level of talent is so high that a healthy campaign is almost sure to keep them a step above the rest of the league, don’t come around all that often. Even when they do come around, they still need to be playing at something close to their peak, and peaks don’t last that long. Until Ohtani, the only player to win more than three MVPs was Barry Bonds, whose regimen for raising and widening his peak has been well documented. Sometimes that’s because of voter fatigue, but often it’s because somebody else popped up with an amazing, undeniable season like PCA’s. Most of the time, the MVP is an already great player for whom everything goes perfectly. They stay healthy and they play not just their best, but over their heads. Think of Ronald Acuña Jr. winning the NL MVP in 2023 with 9.1 WAR, 4.1 more than his next-best total, or Mookie Betts winning the AL MVP in 2018 with 10.2 WAR, 2.8 more than his next-best total.
Generally speaking, since the voting started getting more rigorous in the last couple decades, those are the two categories of players who win MVPs. We see all-time greats who perform like only they are capable of performing, and we see excellent players who put it all together in a blaze of glory. Witt’s 2024 season probably falls into that second category. He wasn’t quite at his defensive or baserunning peak, but he put up his best season at the plate by nearly 40 points of wRC+ and DRC+, and he ended up with an all-timer of a season. His 10.5 WAR tied for the 36th-best position player campaign of all time. His company? Willie Mays and Babe Ruth twice apiece, Barry Bonds, and Rogers Hornsby. Unfortunately, he ran into one of those special players from the first category, in the form of Judge. If Witt had put up those 2024 numbers this year, he’d be en route to a unanimous MVP just like PCA.
But I said “in theory” earlier, and I said it because Witt isn’t done yet. He’s still just 26, and if not for those weeks he missed with back tightness, or a wOBA that’s more than 30 points below his xwOBA, he’d now be wrapping up his third straight seven-plus-win season. He’s elite in every facet of the game and he doesn’t look like he’s in danger of slowing down any time soon. It wouldn’t be much of a shock to see him rediscover his nine- or 10-win form. In other words, there’s at least a chance Witt belongs to that first category of player and not the second.
Earlier I mentioned Acuña and Betts claiming MVPs by putting up the best years of their careers by a long shot. That’s pretty standard. Especially in recent years, it’s awfully rare for a player to take home an MVP award in something other than the best season of their career, unless they also won the MVP in the best year of their career. Leaving those multi-time MVPs out (and excluding 2020 for obvious reasons), here’s the whole list of players who won an MVP in a year that wasn’t their best by fWAR since 2011: Giancarlo Stanton and Paul Goldschmidt.
Goldschmidt put up 6.8 WAR in his 2022 NL MVP season and 7.2 in 2015. In that sense, Goldschmidt fit a third archetype: the established star who doesn’t put up their biggest WAR total, and instead wins MVP as something of a career achievement award. Stanton put up 6.5 WAR in 2017, not quite the 6.8-win campaign he put up in 2014, but he was facing a weaker field, he was more established as a star, and he had the cachet of a 59-homer season. We’re talking about gaps of less than half a win. We had some multi-time winners, but Acuña, Betts, Cody Bellinger, Christian Yelich, Jose Altuve, Kris Bryant, Josh Donaldson, Andrew McCutchen, and Buster Posey all won MVP in the best seasons of their career by fWAR.
Let’s say that Witt does win the MVP this year. For the sake of round numbers, let’s say he closes strong and finishes with 7.0 WAR. That would be just the third-best season of his career, and a full 3.5 WAR below his career-high. Baseball Reference lists MVP winners going back to 1911, and in that time, Witt would become just the ninth position player to win MVP in a season that trailed their best year by such a wide margin. The list of players to do it before him is full of three-time MVPs like Joe DiMaggio, Mickey Mantle, and Mike Schmidt. Not only that, but you’ll note that if Witt does make this list, the only higher number in either column will belong to Mantle:
| Player | MVP Year | MVP WAR | Best Year | Best WAR | Difference | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frankie Frisch | 1931 | 4.1 | 1927 | 9.7 | 5.6 | 
| Mickey Mantle | 1962 | 6.0 | 1956 | 11.5 | 5.5 | 
| Willie Stargell | 1979 | 2.7 | 1971 | 8.2 | 5.4 | 
| Joe DiMaggio | 1947 | 4.8 | 1941 | 9.7 | 4.9 | 
| Freddie Freeman | 2020* | 3.0 | 2023 | 7.7 | 4.7 | 
| Robin Yount | 1989 | 5.3 | 1982 | 9.8 | 4.5 | 
| Andre Dawson | 1987 | 3.5 | 1982 | 7.3 | 3.8 | 
| Mike Schmidt | 1986 | 5.8 | 1974 | 9.4 | 3.6 | 
| Roger Peckinpaugh | 1925 | 2.4 | 1919 | 5.9 | 3.5 | 
The last person to do so was Robin Yount, who won the AL MVP with 9.8 WAR in 1982, and then again with 5.3 WAR in 1989, long before anybody knew that Total Zone considered him the 11th-worst defender in the majors. title: PETE CROW-ARMSTRONG ENTRA EN LA HISTORIA DE MLB | Titansports
author: Lu Llanos
body:
El jardinero central de los Cubs llegó a 45 cuadrangulares y se convirtió en el primero de su posición con 40 jonrones, 30 dobles y 30 robos en una temporada.
Pete Crow-Armstrong alcanzó una combinación estadística inédita durante la contundente victoria 9-1 de los Chicago Cubs sobre los Cincinnati Reds. El jardinero terminó la jornada con tres imparables, dos carreras impulsadas, tres anotadas y una base robada.
Crow-Armstrong conectó su cuadrangular número 45 de la temporada e igualó a Kyle Schwarber en el liderato de las Grandes Ligas. También llegó a 30 dobles y 38 bases robadas, convirtiéndose en el primer jardinero central de la historia con al menos 40 jonrones, 30 dobles y 30 robos dentro de una misma campaña.
La actuación confirmó el crecimiento de un jugador capaz de influir en distintas áreas del juego. A su producción de poder agregó velocidad en las bases y una presencia constante en la ofensiva de Chicago, que se mantiene en plena lucha por asegurar su lugar en la postemporada.
Michael Conforto y Seiya Suzuki también conectaron cuadrangulares por los Cubs. Desde el montículo, David Peterson limitó a Cincinnati a una carrera y tres imparables durante seis entradas. La única anotación de los Reds llegó mediante un jonrón de JJ Bleday.
Chicago continúa entre los principales aspirantes a los comodines de la Liga Nacional. Los Cubs comparten la parte alta de esa clasificación con San Diego, mientras Filadelfia se mantiene cerca después de vencer 7-2 a los Mets.

Pete Crow-Armstrong alcanzó una combinación estadística inédita durante la contundente victoria 9-1 de los Chicago Cubs sobre los Cincinnati Reds. El jardinero terminó la jornada con tres imparables, dos carreras impulsadas, tres anotadas y una base robada.
Crow-Armstrong conectó su cuadrangular número 45 de la temporada e igualó a Kyle Schwarber en el liderato de las Grandes Ligas. También llegó a 30 dobles y 38 bases robadas, convirtiéndose en el primer jardinero central de la historia con al menos 40 jonrones, 30 dobles y 30 robos dentro de una misma campaña.
La actuación confirmó el crecimiento de un jugador capaz de influir en distintas áreas del juego. A su producción de poder agregó velocidad en las bases y una presencia constante en la ofensiva de Chicago, que se mantiene en plena lucha por asegurar su lugar en la postemporada.
Michael Conforto y Seiya Suzuki también conectaron cuadrangulares por los Cubs. Desde el montículo, David Peterson limitó a Cincinnati a una carrera y tres imparables durante seis entradas. La única anotación de los Reds llegó mediante un jonrón de JJ Bleday.
Chicago continúa entre los principales aspirantes a los comodines de la Liga Nacional. Los Cubs comparten la parte alta de esa clasificación con San Diego, mientras Filadelfia se mantiene cerca después de vencer 7-2 a los Mets.

title: Zach Ehrhard, Alek Thomas key Oklahoma City win in finale
author: Eric Stephen
body:
The Oklahoma City Comets closed out their regular season with a 2-1 win over the El Paso Chihuahuas (Padres).
Center fielder Alek Thomas had two of Oklahoma City's eight hits, and his triple drove in the winning run in the eighth inning, allowing the Comets to finish at 89-50, the best record in the Pacific Coast League.
Player of the day
Outfielder Zach Ehrhard hit his 30th double of the season and walked. He scored both runs for Oklahoma City on Sunday, padding his PCL-leading total to 120 runs scored on the season. Ehrhard finished his season hitting .291/.400/.472 with 20 home runs, 28 steals, and 94 walks.
Erhard's 120 runs scored are the most by a Dodgers minor leaguer since Albuquerque Dukes outfielder Lemmie Miller scored 122 runs in 1983.
League leaders
James Tibbs III led the PCL in walks (108), extra-base hits (65, tied with Rockies prospect Zac Veen), and total bases (278), and was second in home runs (30), RBI (107), and runs scored (109).
Ryan Fitzgerald led the PCL in hits (172), including one on Sunday, and doubles (35), and was third in RBI (102). Ehrhard (155) and Tibbs (150) were second and third in hits.
Cole Irvin, who pitched Saturday, led the PCL in ERA (3.33) and wins (12), and his 137 2/3 innings ranked second, two outs shy of the league leader.
Keeping options open
Hyeseong Kim was hitless in four at-bats on Sunday, and finished his regular season hitting just .262/.330/.345 in Triple-A. That was good for only a 79 wRC+ before his 0-for-4 Sunday, after hitting just .259/.323/.328 with an 83 wRC+ in 43 games with the Dodgers this season.
Still, the Dodgers aren't yet ruling out Kim as a potential speedster off the bench, with the ability to play both middle infield spots well in addition to time in center field and even at third base in Triple-A this season.
"My expectation is he will be here in the off week, and potentially be in the conversation for the postseason because he has the ability to run, play defense, and steal a base," manager Dave Roberts said Sunday. "I don't think his offense has been consistent. For us, the at-bat quality that Alex Freeland has been giving us has been very good, he gets on base. For Hyeseong, just trying to find something consistent and to perform consistently. To be quite honest, he just hasn't been as consistent as he can be, but if he can get more consistent with the bat, he can be a big piece."
Transactions
Emmet Sheehan was called up to the Dodgers, as was reliever Kyle Hurt. Right-hander Seth Halvorsen was optioned to Oklahoma City.
Sunday score
The week ahead
Pacific Coast League championship
Game 1, Tuesday: Oklahoma City at Las Vegas
Game 2, Wednesday: Oklahoma City at Las Vegas
Game 3*, Thursday: Oklahoma City at Las Vegas
*if necessary
If the Comets win the PCL title, they would advance to play in the Triple-A championship next Saturday, September 26 on MLB Network, playing the International League champion, a battle between Rochester and Memphis.

title: Mariners News: J.P. Crawford, Andrés Muñoz, and Kade Anderson
author: Becca Weinberg
body:
Good morning! It was so great to see everyone at our fifth annual Tim Cantu MemoriaLL SoftbaLL game yesterday. Thank you to both the new and familiar faces who showed up and helped us reenact a good old fashioned Mariners blow out loss (or win! depending on which team you were on).
The Mariners remain alive with their 2-1 win over the Colorado Rockies yesterday, and will now return home to face the Houston Astros after a day off today. As Ryan mentioned in his recap, the team’s “tragic number” is still at two.
In Mariners news…
- The Mariners have not discussed a new contract with J.P. Crawford, who is in the final year of his four-year/$46.15 million extension.
- Andrés Muñoz is set to receive imaging on his right knee after being forced to exit his outing early yesterday.
- The best start of Kade Anderson’s career so far included seven scoreless innings with three hits, no walks, and seven strikeouts.
Around the league…
- Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman will undergo tests after being hit in the face with a foul ball while in the on-deck circle.
- The Texas Rangers have placed RHP Cal Quantrill on the 15-day IL with a right lat strain.
- The Milwaukee Brewers have set a new franchise win record of 98 with six regular season games still to play.
- Tampa Bay Rays LHP Shane McClanahan will be out for the remainder of the regular season with left forearm tightness.
- The Atlanta Braves have clinched the NL East after an emphatic road sweep of the Houston Astros.
- Despite a 5-1 loss to the Tampa Bay Rays, the Boston Red Sox also clinched a postseason berth yesterday thanks to the Braves’ win over the Astros.

title: Oneil Cruz Places Himself Among Pirates Greats
author: Dominic Campbell; Unknown
body:
PITTSBURGH — Oneil Cruz hasn't had an easy season, but he's still shown why the Pittsburgh Pirates are so on high on his future.
Cruz joined the 20-20 club after his solo home run in the fourth inning against the Kansas City Royals at PNC Park, tying the game at 1-1 in a 4-3 win in the series finale on Sept. 20.
He has 20 home runs and 28 stolen bases in 2026, marking his third straight season joining the 20-20 club, with 20 home runs and 22 stolen bases in 2024 and 20 home runs and 38 stolen bases in 2025.
Cruz becomes the third Pirates player to have three straight 20-20 seasons, along with outfielders Barry Bonds (1990-92) and Andrew McCutchen (2011-13).
Cruz Excelling Since Return From Injury
The Pirates missed Cruz for much of the season due to injury, losing one of their best bats in the lineup.
Cruz fractured his left hand sliding into home plate against the Atlanta Braves on June 6, went on the injured list on June 10 and didn't return to the Pirates until Aug. 17, missing 61 games.
He's been fantastic since coming back, slashing .318/.407/.533 for an OPS of .940 in 29 games, with 34 hits in 107 at-bats, three doubles, a triple, six home runs, 23 RBI and seven stolen bases on 10 attempts.
Cruz has also come up big for the Pirates, with a two-run home run in his first game back to earn a 4-1 win over the Detroit Tigers at PNC Park on Aug. 18 and a go-ahead solo home run off of San Diego Padres All-Star closer Mason Miller in a 1-0 win at Petco Park on Aug. 25.
His power is still among the best in baseball, as he showed with an MLB-best 117.4 mph exit velocity on his solo home run in the 2-0 win over the Chicago White Sox at Rate Field on Sept. 10.
Cruz attributed his recent play to the Pirates' coaching staff and his teammates, leaning on their guidance and support through a tough time and even now, as his hand isn't fully healed.
"It hasn't felt 100% the whole time, but I've decided it was time to play and come back, and I just put my mind into it," Cruz said through interpreter Stephen Morales. "I told myself that if I decide to come back, I'm just gonna do my best every day."
Where Cruz Could've Been With A Healthy 2026
A 20-20 season for Cruz is a solid honor, and even more impressive is that he did it in just 93 games, compared to 132 in 2025.
Cruz should've had a much better season, as he was the first MLB player to join the 10-10 club, and was on pace for 34 home runs and 53 stolen bases before his injury.
He would rank 10th in home runs and first in stolen bases, had he stayed fully healthy and on track and likely in the National League MVP conversations.
Cruz has improved greatly this season, even from the first half, when he hit .264/.350/.472 for an OPS of .822, but especially from his 2025 campaign, slashing .200/.298/.378 for an OPS of .676.
His most impressive change has come against left-handed pitching, batting .323/.373/.476 for an OPS of .849 in 2026, compared to his dismal .102 batting average against southpaws in 2025.
Pirates manager Don Kelly praised Cruz for his growth this season in all areas of his game and for working through his injuries, showing the 27-year-old's maturation in an important part of his career.
"He's had an unbelievable year, and I think we've talked about it in a lot of different ways that it stood out," Kelly said.
"The way that he's grown, being able to separate the offense and defense, play through injuries, play through discomfort, and to to get to 20-20 in 93 games while dealing with what he's dealt with, he worked extremely hard specifically against left-hand pitching, but overall this off-season put himself in a great spot and has followed up with an outstanding year."
Cruz won't get to play in the postseason this year, as the Pirates have already been eliminated and have just six games remaining in 2026.
He's been a big reason the Pirates had a chance this year and if he can stay healthy in 2027, he should play an important role in bringing winning baseball back to Pittsburgh.
"You learn every time," Cruz said on 2026. "This year, not an exception. I learned a lot this year, and also the conversations with the players that been around major league baseball before in the clubhouse, and put [their] advice in play, it helps a lot."
Dominic writes for Pittsburgh Pirates On SI, Pittsburgh Panthers Pn SI and also, Pittsburgh Steelers On SI. A Pittsburgh native, Dominic grew up watching Pittsburgh Sports and wrote for The Pitt News as an undergraduate at the University of Pittsburgh, covering Pitt Athletics. He would write for Pittsburgh Sports Now after college and has years of experience covering sports across Pittsburgh.

title: Astros' Yordan Alvarez Shares Rare Frustration over Brutal Series Against Braves
author: Maddy Dickens; Unknown
body:
There was a point not so long ago that it felt like the Houston Astros were about to run away with the AL West and were actually fighting for the No.2 spot in the American League playoff rankings which would have led to a first-round bye. Well, a lot can change in a week, especially in the AL.
Right now, there is a very mediocre turtle race going on in both the AL West and for the final wild card spot, but right now the Astros are seemingly taking themselves out of that race as they continue to lose games.
After being swept by the Atlanta Braves, at home no less, Houston is three games out of the last wild card slot and one behind the Texas Rangers for the division as they are now two games under the .500 line.
Not too long ago, the Astros had a three-game lead over the Rangers, but boy, have the wheels fallen off the rails as of late. Designated hitter Yordan Alvarez shared his rare public frustrations, via interpreter, with The Athletic's Chandler Rome (subscription required).
Alvarez called a team meeting after the loss on Sunday and called this weekend "three slaps in the face," per Rome. It is very rare that their veteran shows any sort of negative emotion out in the open, but who can blame him?
The Astros are now 4-10 since the first Saturday of September, and they, simply put, are not a postseason team. The ballclub has a day off to regroup before embarking on their final road trip of the season, and they are ultimately feeling October baseball slip through their fingers.
What Went Wrong Against the Braves This Weekend
The first two games of the Braves series never really felt like the Astros were in much control as Houston dropped the opener 6-2 as the Braves hit three home runs with neither the offense nor defense really firing on all cylinders.
However, the biggest heartbreaker was Sunday afternoon at Daikin Park as the Astros went 0-for-3 with the bases loaded, and it was 1-1 going into the sixth inning when Bryan King threw a meatball down the middle of the plate that turned into a three-run homer.

original_title: Astros' Yordan Alvarez Shares Rare Frustration over Brutal Series Against Braves
original_body:
There was a point not so long ago that it felt like the Houston Astros were about to run away with the AL West and were actually fighting for the No.2 spot in the American League playoff rankings which would have led to a first-round bye. Well, a lot can change in a week, especially in the AL.
Right now, there is a very mediocre turtle race going on in both the AL West and for the final wild card spot, but right now the Astros are seemingly taking themselves out of that race as they continue to lose games.
After being swept by the Atlanta Braves, at home no less, Houston is three games out of the last wild card slot and one behind the Texas Rangers for the division as they are now two games under the .500 line.
Not too long ago, the Astros had a three-game lead over the Rangers, but boy, have the wheels fallen off the rails as of late. Designated hitter Yordan Alvarez shared his rare public frustrations, via interpreter, with The Athletic's Chandler Rome (subscription required).
Alvarez called a team meeting after the loss on Sunday and called this weekend "three slaps in the face," per Rome. It is very rare that their veteran shows any sort of negative emotion out in the open, but who can blame him?
The Astros are now 4-10 since the first Saturday of September, and they, simply put, are not a postseason team. The ballclub has a day off to regroup before embarking on their final road trip of the season, and they are ultimately feeling October baseball slip through their fingers.

title: Kyle Tucker rests after fouling ball off right knee
author: Eric Stephen
body:
LOS ANGELES — Kyle Tucker didn't start on Sunday, one day after fouling a ball off his right knee, but the Dodgers right fielder insisted that he felt fine. This was more of a chance to pair a rest day for Tucker with Monday's scheduled off day for the team.
"[The off day] wasn't planned. I just felt that after he took one off the knee, this would have been 10 in a row for him," manager Dave Roberts said Sunday. "He's playing well, played a lot. It's a chance to give him two days, then six in a row to finish the season."
The injury was in a much higher spot on his leg than the right shin fracture that cost him two months on the injured list during the 2024 season while with the Houston Astros.
Tucker did pinch-hit in the eighth inning on Sunday, and he's second on the Dodgers in games played (148), starts (141), and plate appearances (602), trailing only Freddie Freeman in all three categories. Tucker is playing the best baseball of his season at the moment with five home runs in his last 10 starts, hitting .417/.500/.972 since September 9.
Notes
Speaking of playing in the outfield on Tuesday, the Dodgers will likely activate center fielder Andy Pages off the injured list to play in the series opener against the San Diego Padres, after he missed the last 27 games after a fastball broke his left hand on August 21.
Pages at the end of this season will have two years, 155 days of major league service time and will be eligible for salary arbitration for the first time as a Super Two player, among the top 70 percent in service time among major leaguers with two years but not yet three years of service time. MLB Trade Rumors last week projected the cutoff for Super Two players this offseason to be two years, 134 days.
Longtime Dodgers third base coach Joey Amalfitano and knuckleballer Charlie Hough were honored on the field at Dodger Stadium prior to Sunday's game as the 2026 winners of the the Tommy Lasorda I Bleed Dodger Blue Award. This is the fifth year of the award, timed close to Lasorda's birthday, which is Tuesday.

title: Top 9 things at stake in the final week
author: Brent Maguire
body:
The final week of the 2026 regular season has arrived and there is still much to be determined.
While six teams have clinched playoff spots and a few others are close, multiple playoff positions are still up for grabs. And from an individual perspective, there are awards that could be determined in the coming days.
Here’s what is at stake in the final week of the season.
Who will win the AL West and Central?
There’s no telling who will win these two divisions in the American League. The Rays have just about wrapped up the AL East, but the White Sox and Guardians are still battling for the AL Central, while the Rangers and Astros are battling for the West.
This is where things stand. The Rangers lead the Astros by one game in the AL West but Houston won the pivotal tiebreaker against Texas. That means if the two clubs end the season with the same record, the division would go to the Astros.
In the AL Central, the Guardians hold a one-game lead over the White Sox, but Chicago holds the tiebreaker advantage. Any tie between the two clubs means the White Sox would win the division.
Who gets the last AL Wild Card spot?
The AL West and Central battles are directly linked to what’s happening for the final Wild Card spot. It’s very likely that one of those four aforementioned teams will grab the last AL Wild Card spot, unless the Blue Jays have something to say about it. Right now, the White Sox have a fairly comfortable three-game lead over the Blue Jays and Astros.
Could Yordan still win the Triple Crown?
For a while, Yordan Alvarez looked like he might win the MLB Triple Crown, leading the Majors in average, home runs and RBIs. Now, the lefty slugger and presumptive AL MVP winner might merely finish first or second in average, home runs and RBIs. Heading into the final week, Alvarez has a slight edge in average (.313) over Chandler Simpson (.309) and is second in home runs (40) behind Junior Caminero (41) and second in RBIs (99) behind Pete Alonso (105). Alvarez could still snag the AL Triple Crown, but it’ll take a monstrous final week.
Simpson’s unique season and quest for an unusual batting title
Back to Simpson for a second, though. The Rays outfielder is having an excellent season, hitting for average, swiping bases and playing solid outfield defense. What he hasn’t done, though, is hit a single home run. The last hitter to win a batting title without hitting a home run was Rod Carew in 1972. Even if he doesn’t win, he could be the first qualified hitter to bat .300 without a home run since Luis Castillo in 1999.
Will Misiorowski win the ERA title?
It's been a remarkable season for Jacob Misiorowski, who has a 1.86 ERA and 247 strikeouts after Sunday's outing against the Orioles. Assuming he's in line for one more start next weekend -- even if it's abbreviated like his three-inning outing on Sunday -- Misiorowski is in line to join some impressive company. If he can hold his ERA edge over Cam Schlittler's 1.94 mark, he'd join 2021 Corbin Burnes (2.43 ERA in 2021) as the only Brewers to win an ERA title.
If Misiorowski keeps his ERA under two and gets to 250 strikeouts, there's some other fun company he'll join. He'd be just the 13th pitcher (15th instance) since earned runs became official in 1913 to finish a season with a sub-2 ERA and 250-plus strikeouts. The last to do so was Jacob deGrom in 2018.
Will Schwarber or PCA lead the Majors in home runs?
Kyle Schwarber led the National League with 56 home runs last year. As hard as it is to believe, though, Schwarber has never led the Majors in home runs. That could change this year, as the Phillies’ slugger is tied for the MLB lead with 45 homers. The last Phillie to pull that off was Ryan Howard in 2008, when he hit 48 homers and helped lead Philly to a World Series title.
Schwarber, though, has Pete Crow-Armstrong tied with him at the top. The surefire NL MVP has completely taken off this season with 45 homers, 38 stolen bases (more on this shortly), a .949 OPS and his usual excellent center field defense, which has led to an MLB-best 10.5 WAR, per FanGraphs. If PCA surpasses Schwarber, he’d be the first Cub to lead the NL in homers since Sammy Sosa’s 49 homers in 2002 and the first to lead the Majors in long balls since Sosa hit 50 in 2000.
Does PCA get to 40-40?
Crow-Armstrong is making all sorts of history this season. Reaching 10 WAR puts PCA in rarified territory and it seems very likely that the Cubs’ superstar center fielder will be a unanimous MVP winner, something no Cub has ever achieved. Crow-Armstrong is also a mere two stolen bases away from a 40-40 season, something no Cub has done and only six other MLB players have achieved.
Burleson vying to join impressive Cardinals history
Alec Burleson leads the Majors with 111 RBIs, putting him in line for some impressive Cardinals history. He’s looking to become the first Cardinal to lead the National League since Albert Pujols in 2010 and the first to lead the Majors in the category since Joe Torre drove in 137 runs in 1971. His stiffest competition is Cincinnati’s Sal Stewart, who sits at 110 RBIs entering the final week.
How does Verlander's final start go?
Justin Verlander returned to the Tigers for the 2026 season, which will be his final before retiring. Unfortunately, he only made one start in April and hasn't pitched since that point. The good news is he's lined up to pitch on Saturday at Detroit's Comerica Park, which will surely be a feel good moment and send off for the likely future Hall of Famer. Verlander can also add a few more strikeouts to his career total of 3,554.
